verdict_text:
YES

The script drops exactly the 48 buffers (fullmatch on the three per-layer buffer names), casts exactly the 64 projection matrices to bfloat16 via `float().to(torch.bfloat16)` (identical to a direct cast from float16), upcasts every remaining tensor to float32, preserves names, and asserts all four required checks before writing. Sharding at 268,435,456 bytes is delegated to `save_sharded_safetensors`, whose implementation is outside the artifact shown; the call site passes the correct limit and output directory.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
